question: The major carbohydrate of milk is
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lactose**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Lactose** is the main carbohydrate found in milk and milk products.
 
• It is a disaccharide composed of two simple sugars: **glucose** and **galactose**.
 
• Lactose makes up around **4-5% of cow's milk** and provides energy to the body.
 
• The digestion of lactose requires the enzyme **lactase**, which breaks it down into glucose and galactose.
 
• Human milk also contains lactose, playing a vital role in infant nutrition by providing an easily digestible energy source.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lactase deficiency:** Some individuals are unable to digest lactose due to insufficient production of lactase, leading to lactose intolerance.
 
• **Lactose intolerance:** Symptoms include bloating, diarrhea, and abdominal pain after consuming dairy products.
 
• **Other milk components:** Milk also contains proteins like casein and whey, fats, vitamins, and minerals like calcium and potassium.
 
• **Non-dairy alternatives:** People with lactose intolerance often use lactose-free milk or plant-based alternatives like almond, soy, or oat milk.
 
• **Fructose, starch, and maltose:** These carbohydrates are not naturally present in significant amounts in milk; they are commonly found in fruits, grains, and other foods.
